Two round-9 findings on the organizer's record of what it holds. Grouped because both are the same failure — **the system has the information and the surface does not carry it** — and both are small.

## Part 1 — CNT-13: a deliverable is not linked to the talk it belongs to

Rubric item **CNT-13**, weight **1**, `partial` in round 4 and round 9 (0.5 recoverable). Scenario **CNT-S3**. Also a **major** defect this round.

### Acceptance criterion — the rubric's `pass_criteria`, verbatim

> A files view lists the slides.pdf upload with its session and speaker association, upload date, and a version count of 2, consistent with actual uploads; a per-session Files tab, if present, shows the same file (its absence alone does not fail the item if the aggregate library exists)

### The judge's own reasoning (confidence high)

> A central files library exists at /files [...] The slides.pdf row carries FILE "slides.pdf · Upload Session Presentation", SPEAKER "Priya Raman · benevolent.futures+sbek-speaker@gmail.com", STATUS UPLOADED, UPLOADED "Aug 13, 2026", VERSIONS "2 versions" and SIZE 608 B [...] **The gap is the session association the criterion explicitly asks for: the SESSION column reads "— no session attached"**, even though the task-creation form offered a per-assignee "Session for Priya Raman" selector, so the deliverable is not linked to "Taming 40-Minute CI" anywhere in the library.

And the defect: *"Organizers cannot see which talk a deck belongs to, and the library's session search cannot find it."*

### What to build

The association exists in the data — Priya has exactly one accepted session and the deck was requested of her for it. **Derive it when it was not set explicitly**, rather than leaving the column empty because an optional selector was skipped at assignment time. Prefer the explicitly chosen session where one exists; fall back to the speaker's accepted session for this conference when it is unambiguous; say "no session attached" only when it is genuinely ambiguous or absent, and when it is ambiguous, say which choices exist rather than nothing.

The library's session search must find the file by its talk title once the association renders.

Note MRQ-140 already fixed a related bug (file-request tasks assigned via the speaker picker losing their session) and is in this build, so start by checking whether the link is missing at write time or only at read time.

---

## Part 2 — the change history cannot be ordered (minor)

> **`/submissions/:id` — HISTORY panel.** Change-history entries carry date-only timestamps. The HISTORY panel shows "Aug 13, 2026" with no time of day for every entry, so several edits made minutes apart on the same day are indistinguishable and cannot be ordered by their displayed metadata.

The panel's own caption promises "Every change, who made it, and when." A date is not a when for a record that changes several times an hour, and this is the panel an organizer opens precisely when two edits disagree. The underlying rows carry millisecond timestamps already.

Render the time alongside the date, and keep it stable-width (tabular numerals) so the column does not jitter as entries land.

### Acceptance

- The files library shows the session for a deliverable whose speaker has an unambiguous accepted session, and the session search finds it.
- History entries render a time of day and sort unambiguously.
- Regression tests for both.

## Constraints

- Your **own linked worktree**, created as your first act, then `pwd` and `git branch --show-current` to prove it. Never the primary checkout (it is the Lattice board's home); never `mrq-auto-eval*`.
- **Never `git stash` anywhere in this repo** — the stash stack is shared across every worktree.
- **No migration without the operator.** If you conclude one is needed, stop and say so on the ticket.
- **Do not deploy.** An eval round is running and a `.deploy-freeze` marker sits at the primary checkout. Merging is wanted; deploying is not, and is not yours.
- **Elements never jump** — reserve space for anything that swaps.
- Ship a regression test that fails on `main` and passes on your branch.
- Gate serialized. macOS has no `flock(1)`; wrap it: `python3 -c 'import fcntl,subprocess,sys; f=open("/tmp/marquee-gate.lock","w"); fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX); sys.exit(subprocess.run(["npm","run","pr-gate"]).returncode)'`
- PR: `gh pr create --repo Stage-11-Agentics/marquee --base main`.
